claim: Test the complementary tetrahedral rotation on actual native neutron belt points and ordered modes, distinguishing an endomorphism of the fixed carrier from transport into a rotated carrier.
policy: Use the existing source belt geometry and ordered triangle registry, transformed to the established proton Cartesian frame. Apply diag(1,-1,-1) exactly in Q(sqrt(2)). Check point/triangle closure before proposing a permutation of triangle/axis coordinates. Independently construct the rotated points and verify all ordered-mode covariance and Gram identities.
boundary: Failure of fixed-carrier closure does not refute a moving-carrier comparison. Identity of coefficient arrays in transported bases is not an independently sourced PN intertwiner. No E action or cross-context higher-WG restriction is assumed.
stop_condition: Record fixed-carrier closure or its explicit failed point and the moving-carrier cells. Do not manufacture a PN commutator between unbound coordinate types.
